Five BAS mistakes to avoid

By Sam O'Connell · 14 October 2026 · 6 minute read

Lodging your Business Activity Statement every quarter is one of the most routine jobs in running a small business, and also one of the easiest to get wrong. These are the five mistakes we see most often, and how to avoid each one.

1. Claiming GST on items that have none

Bank fees, most residential rent, wages and many fresh foods are GST-free or input-taxed. If your bookkeeping software codes them as taxable, you will claim credits you are not entitled to. Check the tax code on every recurring transaction at least once a year.

2. Mixing personal and business spending

A single card for everything makes the quarter-end reconciliation slow and error prone. Open a separate business account and card, and read our guide to separating your finances.

3. Forgetting the fuel tax credit

If you use fuel in heavy vehicles or machinery, you may be able to claim fuel tax credits on the same BAS. Many businesses leave this money on the table for years.

4. Lodging late

The ATO charges a failure-to-lodge penalty of one penalty unit for every 28 days a statement is late, up to five units. A registered BAS agent gets extra time for most quarters.

Key dates for quarterly lodgers

  • Quarter 1 (July to September): 28 October
  • Quarter 2 (October to December): 28 February
  • Quarter 3 (January to March): 28 April
  • Quarter 4 (April to June): 28 July

5. Not keeping records for five years

You must keep tax invoices and records for five years from the date you lodge. Scanned copies are fine if they are clear and complete.

This article is general information only and is not advice. Talk to your accountant about your situation.
